patterns.name: SHARED_CONSTANTS_IN_TYPES
patterns.description: Move cross-package constants (MODEL_MAP, DEFAULT_TOOLS) to @nomos-ai/types to avoid duplication

patterns.name: SDK_OPTION_PROPERTY_NAMES
patterns.description: Claude Agent SDK has `tools` (base tool set) vs `allowedTools` (auto-allowed without prompting). These are DIFFERENT properties with different purposes.
patterns.recommendation: When creating agent queries, pass tools in options: query({ prompt, options: { tools: [...], allowedTools: [...] } })

patterns.name: SDK_MODEL_ID_FORMAT
patterns.description: Claude Agent SDK uses dated model IDs (claude-opus-4-20250514, claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). Map short names to full IDs via MODEL_MAP.
patterns.recommendation: Create MODEL_MAP object mapping short names (opus, sonnet, haiku) to dated model IDs. Use as lookup table for model selection.

patterns.name: CLI_SCAFFOLD_FIRST
patterns.description: Use established CLI scaffolds (better-t-stack, create-next-app, etc.) for initial project setup rather than manual configuration
patterns.recommendation: For new monorepo setup, use 'bun create better-t-stack@latest' with appropriate flags
patterns.flags_used: --database sqlite --orm drizzle --auth --frontend tanstack-router --addons turborepo biome husky --backend hono --runtime bun --api orpc

patterns.name: ROUTE_TREE_GENERATION
patterns.description: TanStack Router requires route tree generation before TypeScript will pass. After adding new route files (.tsx), run 'vite build' to scan /routes/ directory and regenerate routeTree.gen.ts with type definitions.
patterns.recommendation: Run 'vite build' or 'vite dev' once to generate routeTree.gen.ts before running type checks. After adding new route files, always run 'vite build' before type-checking.
patterns.gotcha: TypeScript check will fail with 'Cannot find module ./routeTree.gen' until first build. New routes won't appear in type definitions until 'vite build' is run.

patterns.name: WORKTREE_ENV_ISOLATION
patterns.description: Git worktrees need separate .env files with absolute paths for DATABASE_URL
patterns.recommendation: Create .env files in worktree during step-00-init with: 1) file: prefix for SQLite URLs, 2) absolute paths using $(pwd) to avoid CWD issues
patterns.gotcha: Relative DATABASE_URL paths break because CWD varies in monorepo execution. Always use: DATABASE_URL=file:$(pwd)/.nomos/nomos.db

patterns.name: BIOME_AUTO_FIX
patterns.description: Biome can auto-fix most formatting and lint issues
patterns.recommendation: Use 'bunx biome check . --write --unsafe' for comprehensive auto-fixes

patterns.name: ZOD_BRANDED_TYPES
patterns.description: Use Zod's .brand<>() for compile-time type safety on primitive IDs
patterns.recommendation: For domain IDs (FeatureId, ProjectId, etc.), use z.string().brand<'TypeName'>() to prevent mixing at compile time
patterns.codeExample:
const FeatureIdSchema = z.string().brand<'FeatureId'>();
type FeatureId = z.infer<typeof FeatureIdSchema>;

patterns.name: STATUS_ENUM_PATTERN
patterns.description: Define status constants as 'as const' objects with derived types and Zod schemas
patterns.recommendation: Use const objects for status values, derive type with keyof typeof, create z.enum() for validation

patterns.name: REGEX_BRANDED_PATTERN
patterns.description: Combine .regex() with .brand<>() for pattern-validated IDs that are also nominally typed
patterns.recommendation: For IDs with specific formats (F001, CAT-XXX), add .regex() before .brand() for runtime validation
patterns.codeExample: const FeatureIdSchema = z.string().regex(/^F[0-9]{3}$/, 'Feature ID must be F001-F999').brand<'FeatureId'>();

patterns.name: ZOD_DEFAULT_NOT_OPTIONAL
patterns.description: Use .default() alone without .optional() - default already handles undefined
patterns.recommendation: When using .default(value), do NOT chain .optional() - it's redundant and creates semantic confusion

patterns.name: NESTED_DEFAULTS_TRANSFORM
patterns.description: Use .optional().transform() to properly apply nested schema defaults when parent field is undefined
patterns.recommendation: When a nested object schema has field defaults that should apply when the parent is omitted or empty, use .optional().transform() instead of .default({})
patterns.gotcha: .default(value) returns value directly without parsing through schema - inner defaults don't apply

patterns.name: SCHEMA_COMPOSITION_PATTERN
patterns.description: Compose schemas by importing existing ID schemas rather than redefining
patterns.recommendation: When creating a new schema that references existing domain types (FeatureId, ProjectId), import and reuse the branded schemas

patterns.name: GOOD_PLANNING
patterns.description: Clear feature scope with specific acceptance criteria leads to zero-retry implementations
patterns.recommendation: Define 3-5 concrete acceptance criteria per feature. Each should be independently verifiable.

patterns.name: FOCUSED_SCOPE
patterns.description: Features that change 3 or fewer core files are completed faster and with fewer issues
patterns.recommendation: Target XS/S-sized features that touch 2-5 files maximum. Split larger features.
patterns.metric: F012: 12 min, 3 files. F013: 4 min, 3 files. F014: 18 min, 5 files. F015: 16 min, 3 files. F016: 13 min, 2 files (XS). F017: 19 min, 3 files (M).

patterns.name: PATTERN_REUSE
patterns.description: Reusing well-known patterns (Hono error handlers, oRPC routing, Bun serve export, health checks, TanStack Router auth guards, route structure) reduces implementation time and errors. F013 completed in 4 min by copying F012 template. F014 copied both F012 and F013. F015 reused F001 scaffold as-is and filled 2 gaps. F016 reused F015 error handling pattern for health endpoint. F017 reused F015 protectedProcedure pattern as base for CRUD router. F018 copied F017 project router template with new entity and transition validation logic. F019 reused feature.ts template with session-specific status transitions and duration tracking. F020 reused route structure from F001 scaffold (beforeLoad auth guards, component layout, query pattern) for 3 new routes.
patterns.recommendation: For all layers: Identify best-in-class template and copy exactly. Database: use CRUD from F012/F013. Server: use Hono error handlers and health check pattern from F015/F016. API: use protectedProcedure pattern from F015 as base for CRUD routers (F017/F018/F019). Frontend: use route structure from F001 scaffold (beforeLoad, component, data fetching pattern) for new routes. Extreme efficiency achieved when existing template matches exactly (F018: 5 min, F019: 58 min including comprehensive test suite, F020: 21 min for 3 routes).

patterns.name: DRIZZLE_TYPE_INFERENCE
patterns.description: Use Drizzle's $inferSelect/$inferInsert for automatic type derivation from schema
patterns.recommendation: Derive repository types from schema rather than manually defining interfaces. This ensures repository types stay in sync with schema changes.
patterns.codeExample:
type ProjectSelect = typeof projects.$inferSelect;
type ProjectInsert = typeof projects.$inferInsert;

patterns.name: DEPENDENCY_VERIFICATION
patterns.description: Always verify external packages are installed before marking feature complete. After adding imports, check package.json and run dev server.
patterns.recommendation: Before completing any feature: 1) List all new imports added, 2) For each external package import, verify it exists in package.json, 3) Run 'bun add <pkg>' for missing deps, 4) Run 'bun run dev' and verify no 'Failed to resolve import' errors
checklist: Identify all new imports in changed files
Separate internal imports (./*, @nomos-ai/*) from external packages
Check package.json for each external import
Run 'bun add <missing>' for any not found
Start dev server and check browser console for resolve errors
Verify feature works in browser before completing
patterns.gotcha: Easy to miss when copying code from other projects or using AI suggestions - packages may exist in source but not in target package.json
patterns.risk_if_ignored: HIGH - feature will crash at runtime even if TypeScript passes

patterns.name: TANSTACK_FORM_ARRAY_FIELDS
patterns.description: Use TanStack Form mode="array" for dynamic list fields (e.g., acceptance criteria). Fields support pushValue()/removeValue() for add/remove buttons with validation on array length.
patterns.recommendation: For list fields in forms, use form.Field(name="arrayField", mode="array") to get field.pushValue(value) and field.removeValue(index) methods. Apply validation on field.state.value.length for min/max constraints.
patterns.code_example: form.Field(name="acceptanceCriteria", mode="array", validators={{onChange: ({value}) => {if (value.length < 1) return "Minimum 1 required"; if (value.length > 10) return "Max 10";}}}) renders array field with pushValue/removeValue.

patterns.name: SHEET_FORM_INTEGRATION_PATTERN
patterns.description: Combine Sheet (sidebar modal) with form components for create/edit workflows. Sheet holds form, handles open state via Zustand UI store. Form prop controls edit vs create mode with conditional mutations.
patterns.recommendation: Use Sheet component to wrap form: <Sheet><SheetContent><FeatureForm feature={selectedFeature} projectId={projectId} onSuccess={() => setSheetOpen(false)} /></SheetContent></Sheet>. Form detects feature prop to conditionally call create or update mutation.
patterns.code_example: feature ? updateFeature.mutateAsync({id: feature.id, data: {...}}) : createFeature.mutateAsync({...data, status: "backlog"}). Mutations both invalidate query key to refresh list.

patterns.name: ZUSTAND_MULTI_ITEM_BOOLEAN_STATE
patterns.description: Extend Zustand UISlice to manage multi-item boolean state (e.g., collapsed columns) using Record<string, boolean>. Use spread operator with computed key to update individual items without replacing entire object.
patterns.recommendation: Pattern: collapsedColumns: Record<string, boolean> = {}. Toggle with: set((state) => ({ collapsedColumns: {...state.collapsedColumns, [status]: !state.collapsedColumns[status]} })). Consumer: const isCollapsed = useAppStore((s) => s.collapsedColumns[status] ?? false)
patterns.code_example: toggleColumnCollapsed: (status) => set((state) => ({ collapsedColumns: {...state.collapsedColumns, [status]: !state.collapsedColumns[status]}, }), undefined, 'ui/toggleColumnCollapsed'). In component: const isCollapsed = useAppStore((s) => s.collapsedColumns[status] ?? false); const toggle = useAppStore((s) => s.toggleColumnCollapsed);

patterns.name: ICON_BUTTON_ACCESSIBILITY_LABELS
patterns.description: Icon-only buttons require context-aware aria-labels that describe the action and reflect current state. Labels should change based on state (e.g., 'Expand column' when collapsed, 'Collapse column' when expanded).
patterns.recommendation: Always pair icon-only buttons with aria-label. For toggle buttons, use state-aware label: aria-label={isCollapsed ? 'Expand column' : 'Collapse column'}. For menu buttons, use consistent description: aria-label='Column options'
patterns.code_example: <Button variant='ghost' size='icon-xs' aria-label={isCollapsed ? 'Expand column' : 'Collapse column'}><ChevronDown className={isCollapsed && '-rotate-90'} /></Button>. Or for menu: <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant='ghost' size='icon-xs' aria-label='Column options' />}><MoreHorizontal /></DropdownMenuTrigger>

patterns.name: ZOD_DISCRIMINATED_UNION_MESSAGES
patterns.description: Use Zod discriminatedUnion for polymorphic message types in WebSocket protocols. Define separate schemas per message type, then union with discriminator field for type-safe routing and validation.
patterns.recommendation: For WebSocket/message protocols with multiple message types, define each as separate Zod schema (wsClientSubscribeSchema, wsClientUnsubscribeSchema, etc.) then use z.discriminatedUnion("action" | "type", [...])
patterns.code_example: const wsClientMessageSchema = z.discriminatedUnion("action", [wsClientSubscribeSchema, wsClientUnsubscribeSchema, wsClientPingSchema]);

patterns.name: PER_CLIENT_SUBSCRIPTION_STATE
patterns.description: Track per-client subscription state in broadcaster using client ID + Set<EventType> map. Handle subscribe/unsubscribe atomically, prevent duplicate subscriptions.
patterns.recommendation: For event broadcasters: 1) Map<clientId, Set<eventTypes>> for subscriptions, 2) subscribe() checks Set.has() before adding, 3) broadcast() filters by client subscriptions
patterns.code_example: const subscriptions = new Map<string, Set<EventType>>(); subscriptions.has(clientId) ? subscriptions.get(clientId).add(type) : subscriptions.set(clientId, new Set([type]))

patterns.name: WEBSOCKET_RECONNECTION_RESUBSCRIBE
patterns.description: On WebSocket reconnect, client automatically resends full subscription list. Server sends "subscribed" response confirming subscriptions. Prevents subscription loss on temporary disconnection.
patterns.recommendation: In client hook: onConnectionChange -> if reconnected, call client.sendSubscription(previousSubscriptions). Server sends back {type:"subscribed", eventTypes:[...]}

patterns.name: HEALTH_CHECK_PATTERN
patterns.description: Async health check endpoint with actual external dependency verification (database connectivity). Returns 200 with healthy status and 503 with unhealthy status.
patterns.recommendation: For all servers: Implement GET /health endpoint with db connectivity check. Response should include: status (healthy/unhealthy), version, database (connected/disconnected), uptime, timestamp.
patterns.testCoverage: Happy path (200), unhealthy state (503), response structure validation
patterns.integration_note: Requires sql primitive export from @nomos-ai/db package. Add to packages/db/src/index.ts: export { sql } from 'drizzle-orm';

patterns.name: oRPC_CRUD_ROUTER
patterns.description: Standard oRPC CRUD router pattern with list, get, create, update, delete procedures, plus entity-specific operations (e.g., updateStatus, appendOutput, getDuration for sessions). Each procedure uses protectedProcedure, Zod input validation, repository integration, and ORPCError for error handling.
patterns.recommendation: For all domain CRUD routers: 1) Define input Zod schemas at top of file (createInput, updateInput), 2) Use protectedProcedure as base, 3) Validate with .input(schema), 4) Handle with .handler(async ({ input, context })). 5) Use ORPCError('NOT_FOUND'|'BAD_REQUEST') for errors. 6) For type-safe IDs, import branded schemas like SessionIdSchema. 7) Add entity-specific procedures that leverage repository helpers (appendOutput, calculateDuration).
keyPoints: Always generate IDs with crypto.randomUUID() in create handler
Type cast Zod objects to Record<string, unknown> when passing to Drizzle for settings/config fields
Use ORPCError with specific codes: NOT_FOUND for missing records, BAD_REQUEST for validation/query errors
Update handlers should build updateData object conditionally (only include fields that changed)
All handlers should be wrapped in try-catch to convert repository errors to ORPCError
Status-changing operations must validate against state machine transition rules
Entity-specific operations (append, calculate, list with filters) should leverage repository helpers
patterns.testCoverage: 36+ tests per CRUD router + additional tests for entity-specific operations covering: create/update/delete ops, validation (string lengths, enum values), error handling (NOT_FOUND, BAD_REQUEST), update partial fields, authentication context, state machine transitions (for entities with status fields), filtering by status/featureId, output append, duration calculation
patterns.integration_note: Router must be exported as named export and imported in apps/api/src/routers/index.ts under appropriate namespace (e.g., sessions: sessionRouter)

patterns.name: TRANSITION_VALIDATION
patterns.description: For entities with status/state machines, enforce valid transitions via a VALID_TRANSITIONS map before allowing status changes. Apply same validation logic to both single and bulk update operations.
patterns.recommendation: Define VALID_TRANSITIONS record at top of router file mapping current state to allowed next states. Check transitions in updateStatus and bulkUpdateStatus procedures before calling repository.
keyPoints: Define transitions at router level (not in repository) for business logic clarity
Check transitions before fetching from DB to fail fast on invalid requests
For bulkUpdateStatus: validate ALL features can transition before updating ANY
Return detailed error messages showing which transitions are invalid and why
Terminal states (VERIFIED, FAILED) should have empty arrays [] to prevent further transitions
patterns.testCoverage: Test valid transitions (backlog→pending, pending→in_progress, etc.), invalid transitions (verified→backlog), bulk operations with mixed validity, error message format
patterns.antipattern_avoided: Without validation, status can be set to any arbitrary value, breaking workflow guarantees

patterns.name: TANSTACK_QUERY_CLIENT_CONFIG
patterns.description: Global QueryClient configuration with sensible defaults for all queries and mutations. Includes staleTime (60s), gcTime (5m), retry logic (3 for queries, 1 for mutations), exponential backoff, and QueryCache error handler with toast notifications.
patterns.recommendation: For all React apps using TanStack Query: Create QueryClient with global defaultOptions for queries and mutations. Implement exponential backoff (2^attempt capped at 30s) for retries. Add QueryCache error handler to notify users of failures via toast.
keyPoints: staleTime 60s: data fresh for 1 minute after fetch
gcTime 5m: keep unused cache 5 minutes before garbage collection
retry 3 for queries: resilient to temporary failures
retry 1 for mutations: don't retry mutations (side effects)
exponential backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, ..., capped at 30s
QueryCache error handler: catches all query errors and notifies user
Invalidation retry: user can retry from toast action
patterns.risk_if_ignored: MEDIUM - without defaults, queries will retry indefinitely, mutations will fail noisily

patterns.name: TANSTACK_QUERY_MUTATION_PATTERN
patterns.description: Mutations with cache invalidation and optimistic updates. Use orpc.{entity}.{method}.mutationOptions({onSuccess}) to integrate with QueryClient. Invalidate related queries in onSuccess callback. Form state managed inline with useState for simplicity.
patterns.recommendation: For all mutations: 1) Use useMutation(orpc.{entity}.{method}.mutationOptions({onSuccess})) for type-safe mutation options, 2) In onSuccess: queryClient.invalidateQueries({queryKey: orpc.{entity}.list.queryOptions().queryKey}), 3) Clear form state after success, 4) Use mutation.isPending to disable button during request.
keyPoints: orpc.{entity}.{method}.mutationOptions() provides type-safe mutation handler
onSuccess callback fires after successful server response
queryClient.invalidateQueries() forces refetch on next access
queryKey must match queryOptions().queryKey for same query
Form state reset in onSuccess ensures clean form after submit
mutation.isPending disables button during request to prevent double-submit
Type-safe mutation: TypeScript ensures input/output types match server
patterns.testCoverage: Test mutations execute successfully, onSuccess callback fires, form state resets, queries invalidate, error state handled, isPending blocks submits, type checking at compile time
patterns.risk_if_ignored: HIGH - without cache invalidation, UI shows stale data after mutations

patterns.name: TEST_ENV_SETUP_PATTERN
patterns.description: Server tests importing env module trigger Zod validation at import time. Need bunfig.toml with [test] preload to set env vars before test imports.
patterns.recommendation: Create bunfig.toml with [test] section: preload = ["./test-setup.ts"] and test-setup.ts that assigns process.env vars
patterns.gotcha: If env vars are not set before imports, Zod validation fails at module load time, causing all tests to fail with cryptic errors

patterns.name: FLEX_SIDEBAR_LAYOUT
patterns.description: Collapsible sidebar using flex layout with width transitions. Sidebar takes fixed width (w-16 collapsed, w-64 expanded), main content uses flex-1 to fill remaining space. Smooth transition with transition-[width] duration-300.
patterns.recommendation: For responsive layouts with collapsible sidebar, use flex parent with fixed sidebar width and flex-1 child. Structure:
keyPoints: Flex layout naturally handles collapsible sidebar - content fills remaining space
Fixed sidebar width (w-16 or w-64) with CSS transition for smooth animation
Main content uses flex-1 to take remaining space, no calculation needed
Transition on width property only, no need for transform
Clean responsive hierarchy: flex parent, sidebar, main content column
patterns.risk_if_ignored: LOW - grid layouts work but are more complex for collapsible sidebars

patterns.name: MOBILE_SIDEBAR_OVERLAY
patterns.description: Mobile-responsive sidebar overlay using fixed positioning. Desktop (md+): sidebar inline relative. Mobile: sidebar fixed overlay with z-50, backdrop fixed with z-40, both shown only when expanded.
patterns.recommendation: For mobile sidebars, use fixed positioning with z-index strategy. Sidebar: 'md:relative collapsed && max-md:hidden !collapsed && max-md:fixed max-md:inset-y-0 max-md:left-0 max-md:z-50'. Backdrop: 'fixed inset-0 z-40 bg-black/50 md:hidden', shown only when !collapsed.
keyPoints: Sidebar: relative on desktop (md+), fixed on mobile when expanded
Z-index: sidebar z-50, backdrop z-40 (backdrop underneath)
Both sidebar and backdrop hidden on mobile when collapsed
Backdrop click triggers toggleSidebar to close overlay
inset-y-0 left-0 covers full height, left edge of screen
Fixed positioning is performant - no JavaScript animation needed
patterns.risk_if_ignored: MEDIUM - without overlay, mobile sidebar overlaps content without dismissal

patterns.name: ZUSTAND_DROPDOWN_INTEGRATION
patterns.description: Dropdown selector connected to Zustand store. Shows selected value from store, updates store on selection. Uses getState() for event handlers that don't need reactive updates.
patterns.recommendation: For dropdowns connected to store: 1) Use selector hook for display value (selected: useAppStore(s => s.selectedProject)), 2) Use getState() in event handler (onClick={() => useAppStore.getState().setSelectedProject(id))), 3) Map store list for options (projects: useAppStore(s => s.projects)).
keyPoints: Selector hooks for data that triggers re-renders (selected project name)
getState() in event handlers for one-off store updates (setSelectedProject)
Show empty state if no selection: 'Select Project' placeholder
Map store list to dropdown items, update on selection
No local component state needed - store is single source of truth
Dropdown menu pattern from shadcn/ui simplifies implementation
patterns.testCoverage: Test dropdown renders, shows selected value, lists projects, handles selection, updates store, shows empty state when no projects
patterns.risk_if_ignored: LOW - without store integration, dropdown becomes disconnected from app state

patterns.name: DND_KIT_KANBAN_INTEGRATION
patterns.description: Drag-and-drop kanban board using dnd-kit with DndContext, DragOverlay, and SortableContext. Requires both PointerSensor (mouse/touch) and KeyboardSensor for full accessibility. Uses closestCenter collision detection.
patterns.recommendation: For kanban boards and task lists, use dnd-kit with both sensors configured for accessibility. Always include DragOverlay for visual feedback.
patterns.risk_if_ignored: LOW - alternative: build custom drag-drop with higher maintenance cost

patterns.name: STATE_MACHINE_VALIDATION_PATTERN
patterns.description: Client-side state machine validation using VALID_TRANSITIONS map to enforce legal status changes before drag-drop operations. Must match backend state machine exactly. Provides user feedback via toast on invalid transitions.
patterns.recommendation: Before building status-based UI, extract VALID_TRANSITIONS from backend router (F018/F019) and copy to frontend. Always validate against backend model.
patterns.gotcha: State machine bugs caught late in QA if backend not checked first. Easy to miss a transition or allow invalid moves.
patterns.risk_if_ignored: HIGH - invalid state transitions at UI level confuse users and can cause data integrity issues

patterns.name: DRAGGABLE_CARD_WITH_USESORTABLE
patterns.description: Draggable card component using useSortable hook. Applies CSS transforms, transition, and opacity based on drag state. Forwards all dnd-kit attributes and listeners to root element.
patterns.recommendation: Every draggable item in dnd-kit should use useSortable with CSS.Transform.toString() for hardware acceleration.
patterns.gotcha: CSS.Transform.toString() required - can't stringify transform directly. All attributes and listeners must be forwarded.
patterns.risk_if_ignored: MEDIUM - without useSortable, items not draggable or missing visual feedback

patterns.name: DROPPABLE_COLUMN_WITH_USEDROPABLE
patterns.description: Droppable column container using useDroppable hook. Shows isOver visual feedback and wraps items in SortableContext with verticalListSortingStrategy for internal sorting.
patterns.recommendation: Every column/container that accepts dropped items should use useDroppable and wrap children in SortableContext.
patterns.risk_if_ignored: MEDIUM - without useDroppable, drop targets don't work and no visual feedback on hover

patterns.name: TANSTACK_QUERY_WITH_MUTATION_CALLBACK
patterns.description: TanStack Query mutation with onSuccess callback that invalidates related queries and shows toast notification. onError callback displays error message to user.
patterns.recommendation: Use mutationOptions() from oRPC with onSuccess/onError callbacks instead of manual state management.
patterns.risk_if_ignored: MEDIUM - without callbacks, UI doesn't update after mutation or show user feedback

patterns.name: EVENT_BROADCASTER_CLEANUP
patterns.description: EventBroadcaster must provide destroy() method and track unsubscribe functions for proper cleanup. Memory leak occurs when subscribers are not removed.
patterns.recommendation: Implement pattern: (1) Track all subscriptions in Set or Map, (2) subscribe() returns unsubscribe function, (3) destroy() iterates all subscriptions and calls cleanup

patterns.name: ASYNC_ERROR_MESSAGE_CAPTURE
patterns.description: In async error handlers, capture error message/stack BEFORE attempting any async operations. Async operations (like DB updates) may fail, masking the original error.
patterns.recommendation: Pattern: (1) catch(error) immediately, (2) extract message/stack synchronously, (3) THEN perform async operations, (4) use captured message in response

patterns.name: WEBSOCKET_BACKPRESSURE_DETECTION
patterns.description: Check ws.bufferedAmount before sending data to prevent buffer overflow and connection drops. High bufferedAmount indicates client cannot consume data fast enough.
patterns.recommendation: Before each ws.send(data): (1) check if ws.bufferedAmount > THRESHOLD (e.g., 1MB), (2) if exceeded, implement backoff (exponential delay) or queueing, (3) log warning

patterns.name: AGENT_LIFECYCLE_COMPLETION_EVENT
patterns.description: Agent stop() must emit agent:complete event for frontend cleanup and UI state management. Without it, frontend may hang waiting for response.
patterns.recommendation: When agent AbortController is signaled: (1) emit agent:complete event with final state, (2) include any accumulated output/errors, (3) frontend receives and cleans up listeners

patterns.name: WEBSOCKET_SEND_SERIALIZATION_SAFETY
patterns.description: Wrap ws.send(JSON.stringify(data)) in try/catch. JSON.stringify can throw on circular references or BigInt values.
patterns.recommendation: Always use try/catch wrapper for ws.send(). If serialization fails, emit agent:error event and log the issue.

patterns.name: REHYPE_SANITIZE_WITH_REACT_MARKDOWN
patterns.description: Use rehype-sanitize plugin with react-markdown to prevent XSS attacks when rendering untrusted markdown content from agent output
patterns.recommendation: For any markdown rendering from untrusted sources (agent output, user content), configure react-markdown with rehype-sanitize: <Markdown plugins={[[rehypeSanitize]]} />

patterns.name: CLIPBOARD_TIMEOUT_CLEANUP
patterns.description: In useCopyToClipboard hook, always clear timeout in cleanup function to prevent memory leaks when component unmounts during copy operation
patterns.recommendation: useEffect with timeout for copy feedback should always return cleanup function that calls clearTimeout()
patterns.gotcha: Without cleanup, timeouts queue up if component re-renders frequently or unmounts before timeout fires

patterns.name: COPY_PENDING_CONTENT_NOT_FINAL
patterns.description: Copy function should include pendingContent (streaming partial messages) in addition to finalized message content
patterns.recommendation: When implementing copy button for streaming/agent output, include both finalized and pending content
patterns.code_example:
const fullText = messages
  .map(msg => (msg.content || '') + (msg.pendingContent || ''))
  .join('\n')
  .trim();
patterns.gotcha: Without pending content, users copying while message is streaming get incomplete output

patterns.name: SEQUENTIAL_MUTATION_CHAINING_WITH_FALLBACK
patterns.description: For complex workflows requiring multiple mutations (createSession -> updateStatus -> sendMessage), chain with .mutateAsync() and error boundaries. If intermediate mutation fails, previous changes may be orphaned—acceptable for MVP with caveat in documentation.
patterns.recommendation: Use async/await pattern with try/catch for clarity: await createSession.mutateAsync(input); await updateStatus.mutateAsync({id, status}); await sendMessage.mutateAsync(...). On error, show toast with specific mutation that failed. For production, consider transaction wrappers or Saga pattern.

patterns.name: DIALOG_WITH_ENUM_SELECT_DROPDOWNS
patterns.description: Confirmation dialogs with multiple Select dropdowns for enum options (Model, ThinkingLevel, PlanningMode). Each Select uses Base-UI pattern with form state management. Defaults from parent feature data.
patterns.recommendation: Create dialog component that accepts feature data prop and spreads defaults to each Select. Use useState for local form state. On confirm, call mutation with values. Pattern matches F028 form architecture.

patterns.name: CONDITIONAL_BUTTON_VISIBILITY_BY_STATUS
patterns.description: Action buttons in detail panels visible only for specific statuses (Start Execution visible when status=pending). Use status check in render logic with conditional className to match panel styling.
patterns.recommendation: In FeatureDetailPanel or similar detail view, check feature.status === "pending" before rendering button. Apply consistent styling with other action buttons.

patterns.name: BACKEND_PRE_IMPLEMENTATION_DETECTION
patterns.description: When Phase 1 scout identifies backend dependency already exists (method, endpoint, service), Phase 3 scope reduces to UI wiring only. Signals lower implementation complexity.
patterns.what_works: Feature completed in 18 minutes with 2 iterations and zero blocking findings.
patterns.actionable: In Phase 1 scout, explicitly document backend readiness: 1) Method exists? 2) Endpoint defined? 3) Resource lifecycle handled? Mark pre_implemented=true for lower risk.

patterns.name: SESSION_RESOURCE_LOOKUP_PATTERN
patterns.description: Pattern for finding active resources by feature ID from list endpoint. Handles: multiple resources per feature, stale status, IDOR checks.
patterns.example_code: const sessions = listSessions(); const active = sessions.find(s => s.featureId === feature.id && s.isRunning); if (active) orpc.agent.stop(active.id);
patterns.what_works: Iteration 2 added proper filtering + ownership check to prevent IDOR.
patterns.gotchas: Must validate: 1) Session exists, 2) User owns session (auth check), 3) Status field is synchronized with isRunning

patterns.name: DESTRUCTIVE_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_PATTERN
patterns.description: Pattern for confirming destructive actions in React: dialog with warning text, disabled button during loading, error toast feedback. Reusable component.
patterns.example_code: const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition(); const handleStop = () => startTransition(() => mutation.mutate(...)); <button disabled={isPending}>
patterns.what_works: Consistent UX across destructive actions. Clear user intent before action.
patterns.implementation_notes: Always include: 1) Warning icon/text, 2) Confirmation button disabled during mutation, 3) Error toast on failure, 4) Success toast on completion
